title: Which inputs that nail accepts silently should warn or fail?
body:
nail exits 0 with an empty result and no warning on each of these inputs. The input survey on nail-d551f7 ran them against the release binary:

| Input | What nail does |
|---|---|
| p7hmm whose last model has no `//` | drops the model; a one-model file gives no queries |
| p7hmm holding only the `HMMER3/f` header line | finds no queries |
| empty, binary, hmm or Stockholm target file | finds no targets |
| text before the first `>` in the target | skips the text |
| a bare `>`, or a `NAME` line with no value | names the record "" |
| p7hmm with no `ALPH` line | assumes amino acids |
| empty `--seeds` file | reports no hits |

## Options

- Fail with an error. A user learns at once that the input was wrong. A script that relies on exit 0 for empty input breaks.
- Warn on stderr and carry on. Nothing breaks, and a warning in a long log is easy to miss.
- Leave each case as it is where HMMER does the same.

I lean to failing on a query or target file with no records and on a truncated last model, and to warning on an empty name. HMMER's behaviour for each case needs checking first.
